author: Fred Pickhardt
title: Major Hurricane Karina Update
text:
Hurricane Karina remains a powerful system with maximum sustained winds of 120 knots (140 mph), but recent satellite imagery shows the storm has begun a gradual weakening trend. While the system is beginning to degrade, it remains a dangerous major hurricane.
Current Status & Present Movement
Position: Near 18.9N, 133.8W (as of 11:00 AM HST, Sept 2, 2026).
Current Intensity: 120 knots (140 mph), down slightly as the storm’s eastern eyewall begins to thin and the eye fills with clouds.
Radius Hurricane Winds: 30 nm
Radius 50 knot winds: 50-60 nm
Max significant Waves: 12-12.5 meters (39-41 feet)
Track: Moving west to west-northwest under the influence of a strong subtropical ridge to its north.
Forecast Track & Significant Changes
Short-Term (Next 48 Hours): Karina will maintain its west-northwestward heading. However, by tomorrow, it will encounter a drier, more stable airmass, which will kickstart a steady weakening process. Winds are forecast to drop below major hurricane strength (under 100 knots) within 36 to 48 hours.
Long-Term (The Weekend): A mid-level low tracking north of the Hawaiian Islands will weaken the steering ridge. This will force Karina to make a distinct turn toward the northwest by Saturday and Sunday.
Dissipation: By Day 5 (Monday, Sept 7), the combination of cooler sea surface temperatures and high wind shear is expected to completely strip the storm of its convection, transitioning it into a post-tropical cyclone with winds down to 40 knots.
